name: Michael Bloomberg
role: Mayor of New York City (2002–2013), founder of Bloomberg L.P. and Bloomberg Philanthropies, 2020 Democratic presidential candidate, UN Special Envoy on climate ambition
summary: A technocratic, data-driven centrist Democrat (a former Republican) who pairs strong support for markets and private enterprise with an activist public-health, gun-control, climate and civil-rights agenda. As mayor he banned smoking in workplaces, capped soda sizes, backed congestion pricing, charter schools and marriage equality, and defended stop-question-frisk and counter-terrorism surveillance, later apologizing for stop-and-frisk. In 2020 he ran on a public option, higher taxes on the wealthy, a $15 minimum wage, abortion rights, strict gun laws and rejoining the Paris Agreement, while rejecting Medicare for All, a wealth tax and socialism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His criminal justice plan reforms rather than abolishes both: it raises police use-of-force standards and rebuilds trust in police, sets a goal of halving incarceration and re-imagines prisons as places for rehabilitation, and as mayor he oversaw the NYPD and defended it.

abortion-legal.rationale: His platform pledges to codify Roe v. Wade, repeal the Hyde Amendment and says 'a woman's right to choose is fundamental'.

central-planning.rationale: Asked about Sanders's agenda in the Las Vegas debate he said 'We're not going to throw out capitalism. We tried. Other countries tried that. It was called communism, and it just didn't work.'

collective-bargaining.rationale: His platform promotes sectoral bargaining where workers face barriers and grants all workers, including gig and franchise employees, the right to organize and bargain collectively.

corporate-influence.rationale: His political reform page seeks to 'eliminate the corrosive power of money in politics' through campaign-finance overhaul, ending pay-to-play and exposing dark money; he says special interests 'corrupt Washington'.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His Greenwood Initiative proposes down-payment aid for 1 million Black homeowners, 100,000 new Black-owned businesses and $70 billion for distressed neighborhoods to address the legacy of discrimination, and he promises to 'right the wrongs of institutional racism'.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: His Advocate op-ed notes that for decades same-sex relationships were a crime, saying it is hard to imagine now that someone could go to prison for years for being intimate with a loved one in private.

death-penalty.rationale: His expanded criminal justice plan calls for 'abolishing the death penalty once and for all', and his 2022 column says there is no evidence harsh sentencing, including the death penalty, lowers murder rates.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: His 2020 plans expand the Earned Income Tax Credit, guarantee housing vouchers for households below 30% of area median income and widen aid, the opposite of cutting. As mayor he took pride in a falling welfare caseload (2013 State of the City), which the 2020 platform does not repeat.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: In 2013 he rejected comparing stops to census demographics as 'not rational' and said NYPD stops 'follow the crime'; he later apologized for stop-and-frisk's impact but did not retract that point.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: In Miami in 2020 he said his three terms as mayor of the most diverse city taught him that 'diversity is our strength', quoting King that it 'ties us together into a single garment of destiny'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His platform makes climate 'one of his highest priorities': rejoin the Paris Agreement on day one, cut carbon pollution 50% by 2030 and reach net zero by 2050 or sooner, with new federal pollution limits and standards.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His foreign policy page says 'the greatest source of American strength abroad is... our partnerships' and promises to repair frayed relationships and deter rivals with regional coalitions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His equal rights page commits to 'freedom and full equality for all' and equal rights and opportunity for everyone, and he recalls his father's lesson that discrimination against anyone threatens all.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He repeatedly praises diversity and immigration ('diversity is our strength'), and says people of every faith and background are New Yorkers.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: His 2020 clean-power plan ends all subsidies for fossil fuels, puts a moratorium on new fossil fuel leases on federal lands and offshore, and phases out power-sector emissions.

expand-nuclear.rationale: At the Council on Foreign Relations in 2015 he said 'nuclear makes a lot of sense' for climate and criticized the governor's push to close Indian Point; his 2020 platform did not call for new plants.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: His financial reform plan introduces a 0.1% tax on all financial transactions to raise revenue to address wealth inequality.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He wrote that he wants to make 'the system fairer and more progressive', and his plan raises top rates and ties capital-gains rates to ordinary rates, the opposite of a flat tax.

free-public-college.rationale: Mixed: his plan makes two-year public college tuition-free for all, but four-year public college only tuition-free for the lowest-income students, with affordability measures for the middle class.

free-trade.rationale: His 2020 platform seeks 'high-standard trade deals', 'fair trade agreements that open markets' and cooperation with the WTO, and he has called protectionism counterproductive and opposed Trump's tariffs.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His platform pledges to fight for the Equality Act, which bans discrimination in employment, housing, credit and public accommodations, and he points to extending NYC's anti-discrimination law to gender identity.

future-generations.rationale: Launching PlaNYC he said that when we put our children to bed, 'they are the ones who will pay the heavy costs of our inaction', and committed to cut the city's carbon footprint by 30%.

government-nudges.rationale: His administration's Board of Health rules, which he announced and defended, post calorie counts in chain restaurants, ban trans fats, post restaurant letter grades and cap sugary-drink servings at 16 ounces, a limit that 'does not limit anyone's consumption; it just requires them to think about whether they really want more'.

harm-principle.rationale: His soda-size limit restricts what adults may buy for the sake of their own health: he said 'we have a responsibility as human beings to do something, to save each other, to save the lives of ourselves', and he also banned trans fats and smoking in parks and beaches; he signed the 2002 workplace smoking ban.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: His 2020 climate platform opens 'Fossil fuels are polluting the air we breathe and changing the world we live in' and says that President Trump 'denies climate change and works to support fossil fuel industries, making the problem worse', tying the warming to burning fossil fuels.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: His All-In Economy plan enhances the Earned Income Tax Credit and pays it monthly, and he extended the idea to low-income workers without children in New York's Paycheck Plus programme.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His tribal plan promises to affirm tribal sovereignty, reaffirm Indian Country land rights and elevate tribal authority.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: At AIPAC in 2020 he called Israel the Jewish people's 'ancestral homeland', 'the world's only Jewish state', and said Israel must remain a prosperous, secure and stable Jewish democracy.

limit-growth.rationale: PlaNYC frames the goal as absorbing 'the coming growth' while strengthening the economy, health and quality of life, treating growth and environmental protection as compatible rather than limiting growth.

limit-guns.rationale: His platform requires a permit before any gun purchase, universal background checks, a 48-hour wait, an age-21 minimum, red flag laws, an assault weapons and magazine ban and secure storage; he co-founded Mayors Against Illegal Guns and as mayor urged Congress to ban assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, saying this falls within the Second Amendment.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: His 2020 plan seeks to reverse 'an overly punitive' sentencing legacy, reform excessive sentencing and end federal cash bail, rather than add fixed statutory sentences.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: he calls himself a big believer in capitalism, rejected throwing it out in the 2020 debate, and in 2026 argued that political ownership of firms destroys market competition and, in 2022, that the private sector is 'the most powerful force we can muster' on climate. His mayoralty and platform also use heavy regulation and public programmes, so he does not state a general preference for markets over governments.

military-superiority.rationale: His foreign policy page calls for strengthening 'all elements of American national power', investing in the technologies needed to win on the battlefield of the future and keeping US advantages in AI and quantum computing against rising powers such as China.

nation-first.rationale: He says 'America's responsibility is to be the leader in the world', works with China and India on climate, and wants to rebuild alliances and cooperate on global problems, though he frames cooperation as in America's interest.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His mayoral record (smoking, trans fat and soda rules, public health programmes, education reform) and his 2020 platform (public option, transfers, regulation) go well beyond defence, justice and property protection.

no-bailouts.rationale: His financial reform plan aims to end the need for 'taxpayer bailouts' by strengthening safeguards, and his 2026 column warns that firms 'too big and bloated to fail' leave the public on the hook for bailouts.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: He wrote that 'if you have an opportunity to help, you have an obligation to act' and says he has committed to giving away virtually all his wealth in his lifetime.

open-borders.rationale: His immigration plan keeps border enforcement, with 'smart security measures', upgraded ports of entry and sensible enforcement priorities, alongside a legal system with place-based visas rather than open borders.

open-government-data.rationale: As mayor he promised to make city data public so 'the tech community can hold us accountable', and wrote that the public should be given access to city data to demand better from leaders.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: His LGBTQ+ plan celebrates the repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell, would restore honorable discharges and benefits to those discharged for being LGBTQ+, and would reverse the transgender military ban.

property-fundamental.rationale: As mayor his administration pursued the Willets Point redevelopment while reserving eminent domain as a tool, saying it would rather cut deals than condemn (a news report of the record, not his own words).

racial-franchise.rationale: His voting-rights plan aims to stop states excluding African Americans and other minorities and to reinvigorate the Voting Rights Act.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His Greenwood plan ties federal housing funds to progress in reducing segregation and attacks zoning and government policies that segregated communities.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He called for a $15 federal minimum wage indexed to earnings growth and said of New York's $15 wage that it is 'as it should be nationwide'.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His platform would 'open America's doors' to immigrants the economy needs, give an earned pathway to citizenship to 11 million undocumented people and raise the refugee target to 125,000; as mayor he urged Congress to welcome 'more of the best and brightest'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His financial reform plan promises 'common sense regulation' of banks, a restored and strengthened CFPB, a corporate crime unit at the Justice Department, and rules on payday lending and overdraft fees; his gun plan repeals the industry's liability shield.

rehabilitation.rationale: His criminal justice plan sets out to 're-imagine prison as a place for rehabilitation from day one', with education, job training, drug treatment and a 50% cut in the prison population by 2030.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He called for Trump's removal by impeachment, saying the House did its Constitutional duty and calling the president's conduct a 'gross abuse of power'.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: In a September 2025 column he said using law enforcement to crack down on 'hate speech' would run afoul of the First Amendment.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He wrote that in business and city hall his rule is 'In God we trust. Everyone else: bring data', and criticizes government for burying data beneath 'political considerations and ideological attachments'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He came out for marriage equality in 2005, lobbied Republican state senators to pass it in 2011, officiated at one of the first weddings and said it 'has made our City more open, inclusive and free'.

separate-church-state.rationale: Defending the Park51 mosque he called it 'an important test of the separation of church and state' and said government 'must never choose between religions, or favor one over another'.

separated-powers.rationale: He told Texas Democrats that flipping the House restored 'at least some of the oversight of the president that the founding fathers had designed into the Constitution' and said the House 'did its Constitutional duty' by impeaching Trump.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: His reproductive rights plan directs federal funding to science-based sex health education.

social-market-economy.rationale: He defends capitalism (debate: 'We're not going to throw out capitalism') while his platform adds a public option, minimum wage, paid leave and financial rules, a market economy with social protection and regulation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He said Trump 'has no respect for the rule of law' and framed a commander-in-chief's respect for the rule of law as essential.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mixed: his 2026 column calls government equity stakes in firms for supply-chain or national-security reasons 'misguided', but his 2020 platform has the federal government fund R&D growth hubs and quadruple clean-energy R&D.

state-harmful.rationale: He treats government as a useful provider and regulator: in the debate he said he pays his taxes happily 'because I get something for it', and his career in office was spent expanding public health, safety and education programmes.

student-debt-relief.rationale: His plan halves the cap on federal loan payments and forgives remaining balances tax-free after 20 years, relief short of general cancellation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As mayor he invested 'heavily in our counter-terrorism infrastructure, including a network of cameras', and in April 2013 defended NYPD counter-terrorism intelligence gathering against oversight legislation, warning terrorists might succeed if it undermined that work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In the debate he said Trump's tariffs are 'hurting us', his farm plan calls Trump's trade war with China ill-advised for gutting markets for American farmers, and in 2026 he called the Jones Act 'one of the most counterproductive protectionist measures of the last century'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His New York Times op-ed says wealth passes between generations 'with little or no tax due'; his plan ends the loophole that lets growth in an estate escape tax at death and reforms the estate tax.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2020 plan restores the 39.6% top rate, adds a 5% surtax on income above $5 million (a 44.6% top rate), taxes capital gains above $1 million as ordinary income and raises the corporate rate to 28%; he wrote that he agrees with raising taxes on 'wealthy people like me', though he opposed a wealth tax.

term-limits.rationale: Mixed: he introduced and signed the 2008 charter change extending New York City's limit from two to three terms so that he could run again, after serving three terms as mayor.

treaties-binding.rationale: His tribal platform says the federal government must honor the special treaty and trust relationship with Native American tribes.

unions-good.rationale: His labor platform says falling union membership has deprived workers of a vital voice for fair wages and protections, and he pledges to strengthen union protections, ban right-to-work laws for private-sector unions and back sectoral bargaining.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2020 health plan states the aim of universal coverage: a Medicare-like public option paid by premiums, with subsidies for people of modest means and an expanded ACA, while letting people keep private insurance. He rejected Medicare for All, so the state guarantees access without providing all coverage itself.

voter-id.rationale: His voting plan lists 'voter ID restrictions' among practices that undermine democracy and proposes uniform national standards that make voting easier.

notes:
Evidence comes from his own words and record: the 2020 platform pages, debate and speeches, op-eds and columns (2015-2026), and mayoral texts and laws. Where his views changed, the recent position was used: after the February 2020 debate he reversed on non-disclosure agreements, and in 2019 he apologized for the stop-and-frisk policy he had defended as mayor in 2012-2013 (the 2013 words are kept for the specific statements they bear on, at lower confidence). 2020 campaign pledges are his stated programme, not governing record, since he never held national office; where the 2020 platform differs from his mayoral years, the 2020 position is used as the more recent one. Term limits are a mixed case: he supported limits but sought and signed an extension to three terms for himself in 2008. Evidence about nearby but different questions (decriminalizing marijuana versus legalizing all drugs, tariff or ownership stakes in AI versus public ownership of utilities, Israeli two-state policy versus national self-determination in general) was left null.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14): brought to rules 7 with no changes needed; added government-nudges from his city health rules. nyc.gov now returns 403 to automated fetches, so the 2013 press release was read in its Wayback copy.
